Addon.description: A skill, an MCP server or an instruction file an agent gets.

about.description: Its own line about itself (a skill's description).

agents.description: The ids of the agents that get it.

copies.description: Other places the same one sits in (a second copy of a skill's folder).

fixed.description: The agents among `agents` that get it whatever the switch says: they have no way to leave it out of one chat.

key.description: What `addons.set` takes to switch it for the project: its own ("skill:tabbit", "server:claude_ai_Gmail", "kelp:kelp-vm") or its plugin's ("plugin:sales", which switches all of that plugin's). nil: nothing switches it.

loaded.description: In the chat asked about: true when it loaded there; nil when no chat's own record says.

off.description: Off for this project: a chat started from now on doesn't get it.

origin.description: Where it comes from, as the person would name it: a folder ("~/.agents/skills"), a file, a plugin, "claude.ai".

problem.description: Why it doesn't work, in a few words ("Doesn't start: no such file").

signIn.description: A server that waits for a sign-in: it offers nothing else until then.

tokens.description: What it adds to every request of the chat, estimated from the chat's own record; nil when unknown.

Addon.Source.description: Who brought it: Kelp (its own skills), the person (their folders and settings), the project (its files), a plugin of the agent's, the agent's account (claude.ai's skills and connectors), or the agent itself (built in).

Addons.description: What `addons.list` answers. `chat`: the list is what that chat reported at its start (Claude Code writes it down); false when it's only what the files say a new chat would get.

AgentCommand.description: A command an agent ran with its shell tool (Claude Code's Bash, Droid's Execute), as its hooks tell it (`kelp hook command`): what it ran, how that went and the end of what it printed. The session's tab lists them (`session.commands`), its row shows the one running.

description.description: The agent's own words for it ("Run the tests").

output.description: The last `outputLimit` bytes it printed (stdout, then stderr).

AgentSessionInfo.description: One resumable conversation of a CLI coding agent, read from its on-disk transcript (AgentData reads them).

messageCount.description: Exact for small files; extrapolated from the head and tail for large ones.

id.description: nil: not found, or it printed no version (`latest`: not on npm, or npm isn't installed).

ArtifactItem.description: An artifact as the Artifacts panel shows it (`ArtifactsEvent`): its record, what opens it, and what its file says now.

modified.description: When its file was last saved; nil for a page on a service.

points.description: A review's points, and how many have a pick.

preview.description: What its preview shows: its file, or Kelp's copy of a page on a service (`Artifacts.pageCopy`); nil for none.

target.description: Its file, or its page on the service (`Artifacts.target`).

versions.description: Its kept versions, oldest first; `changed`: the file differs from the last of them (written since, or none kept yet).

ArtifactVersion.description: A page as one turn of its agent left it: `versions/<n>.md` (or `.html`) beside it, named by the prompt that started the turn.

Artifacts.Kind.description: The kinds Kelp makes on this Mac, and the file each one is: Markdown, or a page of HTML for what Markdown can't draw.

ArtifactsEvent.description: A watched workspace's artifacts (`.kelp/artifacts`), latest change first, pushed when that folder changed.

ahead.description: Commits to push: past the upstream, or with none, on no remote branch (what the graph marks "not pushed yet").

on.description: `why`: "Vite in package.json", "no web app found"… `choice`: the project's own, nil when it follows Settings. `hint`: off, but the agent is told where the guide is (not when Settings says Never).

CIRuns.Failure.description: One thing that broke: a test, or a compiler's error (no `test`), with where and what, read from a job's log.

file.description: Relative to the project where the log says enough to tell.

CIRuns.Report.description: What a failed log says. `failures` comes from the whole log, before `log` keeps only its tail.

exitCode.description: For a log in no known format: how it ended, and the lines before that.

more.description: Failures left out past the cap.

tests.description: Tests that ran, when the log counts them.

number.description: The forge's count of the workflow's runs, the commit, which try this is; when this try began and last changed.
Its place in the job, which a link to the step names.

CIRuns.Workflow.description: A workflow you can start by hand (`on: workflow_dispatch`), with the inputs its form asks for.

ChangedEvent.description: Projects or workspaces changed: read the lists again. The params are just the word. Still sent for clients that read lists; the changed records themselves come as `event.repo` / `event.worktree` / `event.removed`.

CloneEvent.description: A line of `git clone`'s progress, to the connection that started the clone.

CodeAction.description: A fix or refactoring a server offers at a place, with what it changes.

CodeCompletion.description: One completion: what the list shows and what goes in.

kind.description: "method", "keyword"…; its documentation; whether `insert` has tab stops; what it replaces, and what else it changes.

CodeEdit.description: A server's edit: `text` from `line`, `column` to `endLine`, `endColumn`, all 0-based, in UTF-16 units.

CodeFileEdit.description: One file's part of a server's change, `edits` as it gave them.

CodeProblem.description: An error or warning a language server found: from `line`, `column` to `endLine`, `endColumn`, all 0-based, in UTF-16 units.

CodeSignature.description: A call's signature as the cursor stands in it: `label`, with the argument being typed at `active` (UTF-16 offsets in it).

CodeSymbol.description: A name a file defines: what it's called, what it is ("class", "function"…) and its 1-based line. `path`: the file, in a project-wide list.

CommitDetails.description: A commit's message body (the subject is the graph's), its author's email, and its size against the first parent.

ContextEvent.description: Nil usage: not known (not Claude Code, ended, just compacted).

databases.description: The server's databases, for the sheet's pop-up; empty for a file.

environment.description: Its environment as the user (or the app it came from) said; nil: Production when `production`, else Local.

group.description: The group it was kept in where it came from (TablePlus' group, DBeaver's folder), for "All my projects".

name.description: Its name in the project: what `kelp db --db` and the tab's address use.

passwordIn.description: Where its password still is, outside Kelp: another app's keychain item ("<service>\u{1F}<account>"), read the first time the database is opened (macOS asks then, once) and kept in Kelp's own from there.

production.description: Agents only read it, whatever `access` says: on a host that isn't this Mac, or named so.

source.description: The file it was found in, relative to the project ("compose.yaml", ".env.production"); nil: added by hand.

ssh.description: A host of ~/.ssh/config the server is reached through (a port forwarded over Kelp's shared connection).

ssl.description: TLS to the server, libpq's words: "disable", "require"; nil or "prefer": when the server offers it.

DatabaseInfo.Access.description: What agents may do with it: not see it, read it, change it once the user allows each change, change it freely.

DatabaseInfo.Stage.description: Which kind of database it is, as TablePlus and TablePro tag theirs: its colour everywhere it shows (green, blue, orange, red). Production is the one agents only read.

DatabaseRun.description: A statement run on a project's database, by an agent (`session`) or the user.

error.description: The database's error, or why it didn't run.

session.description: The agent's session; nil: the user's.

DatabaseSchema.description: A database's tables, as an agent reads them before it writes a query.

functions.description: The database's own functions, by name ("schema.name" outside the default schema); nil where Kelp doesn't read them.

bytes.description: Its size on disk with its indexes, and its comment, where the database says them.

kind.description: "view" for a view (or a materialized one); nil: a table.

rows.description: Its rows: counted for SQLite, the planner's estimate elsewhere.

DatabasesEvent.description: A watched workspace's databases and their latest runs, newest first: pushed when one runs or a database changes.

library.description: "All my projects": the user's own, which no agent sees until one is used in a project (`db.use`).

Delivered.description: How many Kelp windows were told.

DevServerEvent.description: A dev server in a workspace printed its local URL.

author.description: The agent that wrote it (a reviewer's finding); nil: the user.

commit.description: HEAD when it was written: what the old file's line numbers are counted in.

onCommit.description: The past commit whose diff it's on (full hash); nil: on the folder's changes.

side.description: "old": the lines are removed ones, numbered in the old file; nil: the new file's (or a comment from before sides).

noNewline.description: The file's last line, with no newline after it (git's "\ No newline at end of file").

category.description: What the library files it under: tools, themes, icons, languages, agents or integrations. nil: an index from before categories.

files.description: Each file's SHA-256 as reviewed, by path in the folder: an install takes these bytes or nothing.

requires.description: Commands it needs on PATH (an extension without them stays inactive).

reviewed.description: false: found on GitHub by its `kelp-extension` topic, never reviewed; shown apart, with a warning.

source.description: The reviewed folder on GitHub, at its commit: what `extension.fetch` takes.

stars.description: Its repository's stars, and how many it gained in the last week (what the unreviewed list is sorted by).

header.description: Raw `diff --git` / `---` / `+++` lines, needed to rebuild patches for hunk staging.

latin1.description: The file isn't UTF-8: its text was read byte for byte (Latin-1), and patches go back the same way.

tooLarge.description: Its changes are past what one reply carries (`Git.diffBudget`): no hunks, only the header. Asked for alone, it may fit.

FileEvent.description: A watched file's version now: the stamp `files.read` and `files.write` give (nil: it's gone, or isn't a file). Only the stamp: whoever holds that version (the app's own save) has nothing to read. A touch is a new version too. `problems`: what its language server says is wrong with it, pushed as the server says it.

FilesEvent.description: A watched workspace's files as `files.list` gives them, and what git ignores (`files.ignored`), pushed when that changed. `error`: they couldn't be listed.

stamp.description: What's there now; its text nil when that isn't UTF-8.

GitEvent.description: A watched workspace's git, read again after its files changed. `error`: git couldn't say (not a repository…).

branchFiles.description: What its branch committed since it left the project's base branch (nil on the base itself): with `changes`, every file it would bring in, which another folder of the project may be changing too.

name.description: `bucket` is gh's category of `state`: pass, fail, pending, skipping, cancel.

title.description: `type` is Issue, PullRequest or DraftIssue; drafts have no url.

headRefOid.description: The head commit when the list was read (GitHub's): a merge goes ahead only while it is still the head.

mergeState.description: GitHub's word for whether it can merge: CLEAN, BLOCKED, BEHIND, DIRTY (conflicts), UNSTABLE, DRAFT, UNKNOWN.

path.description: path/line are nil for top-level review bodies.

GitWebPages.Pages.description: `forge`: "github" | "gitlab" | "bitbucket"; `ci`: Actions / Pipelines; `pulls`: pull or merge requests.

GraphCommit.description: One row of the commit graph (VS Code's Source Control Graph). Lines are lane pairs: `top` runs from the row's top edge (lane `[0]`) to its middle (lane `[1]`), `bottom` from the middle to the bottom edge.

cpu.description: Busy share of all cores, 0–100, over a moment of the read. Linux only.

error.description: Why the last connection failed, in ssh's words; nil once one worked.

memory.description: Bytes used and in all. Memory and swap: Linux only.

processes.description: The busiest processes, and every one of Kelp's agents, by CPU.

tmux.description: Kelp's tmux sessions there (`Tmux.isOwn`), with the Kelp session each belongs to, if one does.

uptime.description: Seconds since boot; the 1, 5 and 15 minute load averages. Linux only, the load also on macOS and BSD.

local.description: Reached only from the server itself (127.0.0.1, ::1): forward it to use it here.

command.description: The program's name, and its whole command line.

memory.description: Resident bytes; seconds it has run.

session.description: The Kelp session it runs under (its tmux pane's), if any.

ImportOutcome.description: What an import did: the databases it kept, how many came with their passwords, how many will ask for theirs when first opened, and the ones it couldn't keep (with why).

denied.description: The user said Don't Allow to macOS: the rest came without their passwords.

ImportSource.description: An app (or a file of a standard's) on this Mac that keeps database connections Kelp can bring in.

id.description: "tableplus", "dbeaver", "datagrip", "sequelace", "beekeeper", "dbgate", "pgpass", "pgservice", "mycnf"; "pgadmin" and "navicat" are read from a file the user picks (their export).

passwords.description: Where its passwords are: "keychain" (macOS asks for each), "file" (readable without asking: Kelp asks first), "none" (typed when first used).

ImportedDatabase.description: One connection as another app keeps it, read as Kelp would keep it.

id.description: Its id where it comes from.

known.description: Kelp has one at the same address already: off in the list.

note.description: What Kelp can't do the same way ("SSH through a password: set SSH by hand"), or why it's Production.

LimitHit.description: A plan limit that stopped a session's turn.

at.description: When it stopped: `resets` is read from here, so "3pm" stays today's once that has passed.

resets.description: When it resets, as the agent printed it ("3:40pm", "Oct 20 at 5am"); nil when it didn't say.

LineStats.description: Lines added / removed in the working tree (staged, unstaged and new files) against HEAD, split by what kind of file.

LinearState.description: `type` is Linear's state category: triage, backlog, unstarted, started, completed, canceled.

MachineEvent.description: What runs in a machine; nil while it isn't running.

OutputEvent.description: What a session printed, to a client attached with JSON (`session.attach`), not as a byte pipe.

PortBusyEvent.description: A run couldn't start: what it printed says `port` is taken.

PortsList.Port.description: A port a process of one of the workspace's sessions listens on; on a remote project's host, one in its folder.

host.description: On a remote project: its host, the port on this Mac once forwarded, and true when the host can't be asked (this is its last answer).

port.description: `session`: "" when it can't be told. `pid` 0: none, a forwarding asked for by hand.

PublishedPage.description: What a publishing tool sent of the page itself: Kelp keeps a copy of it beside the link, for the panel's preview (Kelp's tabs can't sign in to the service, so they can't show the page there).

edits.description: Changes to the last version (`edit_version`), applied to the copy.

file.description: A file on this Mac that holds it (`publish_files`: its index.html, or a canvas's first board).

QueryResult.description: What a statement gave: its columns and rows (text, nil for NULL), cut at the asked limit.

changed.description: Rows a change touched; nil for a read.

cut.description: Rows left out for their size (past what Kelp keeps of a result's cells, 1 MB): a larger `limit` gives no more.

id.description: Its entry in the database's history (`db.result`).

total.description: The rows it gave, `rows` or more: past the limit they're counted only up to what Kelp keeps.

RemovedEvent.description: A project, workspace or session record that's gone (a project takes its workspaces with it; their sessions each say so).

copyFiles.description: Glob-ish file names copied from the repo into each new worktree (e.g. ".env").

removable.description: Nothing uncommitted or untracked, not locked, not one of Kelp's workspaces (those go with Delete Workspace).

Routine.description: An agent on a schedule: at its time the daemon starts `agent` with `prompt` in the routine's own workspace (in the project's folder, made at its first run), and keeps how each run went.

checked.description: Due times up to here are handled: run, missed, or before the routine was on.

id.description: Empty: a new one (routine.set gives it an id).

onWake.description: A run missed while the Mac slept or Kelp wasn't running: once when it's back (true), or skipped.

time.description: Minutes after midnight; hourly: minutes past the hour.

weekday.description: Weekly: 1 Sunday … 7 Saturday, as Calendar counts.

Routine.Run.description: One run: its agent's session, and how it went.

due.description: When it was due; Run Now: when it was asked for.

summary.description: The agent's first line when done, what it asks, why it failed.

RoutinesEvent.description: Every routine and their runs of the last two weeks, newest run first: routine.list's answer, and `event.routines`, sent whenever one of them changes.

RunOption.description: Something the project's own files say can be run: a package.json script, a Makefile target, a compose service, a Python app… (`run.detect`). It runs only when someone picks it (`run.start`), never because a project was opened.

detail.description: What the entry says, when that isn't the command (a script's body, a service's port).

folder.description: Where it runs, inside the workspace ("" is its own folder).

id.description: "folder|file|name": the same while the file keeps the entry, so a choice can be remembered.

missing.description: The program it needs that isn't on that machine's PATH.

container.description: Docker's id and name for it ("shop-db-1"), and its image ("postgres:16").

database.description: Its address as this Mac reaches it, the user and database its environment names.

digest.description: Of exactly the text read: `scripts.trust` trusts what was shown, not a later version.

ServerEntry.description: An MCP server as Kelp keeps it and as the agents' own files spell it (`mcpServers`): a program it starts (`command`, `args`, `env`) or an address it calls (`url`, `headers`).

argv.description: Launch options, kept so "Restart" reproduces the session.

awaiting.description: The one of them it waits for (a test run, not a server): its tab glows for it while it works. A Stop says which; one sent to the background mid-turn counts until then, unless it looks like a server. nil when it waits for none.

background.description: Commands it started in the background that still ran when its turn ended (a test run it waits for, a dev server).

browser.description: Whether Claude Code got Kelp's browser skill, and why ("on · Vite in package.json"); nil for agents without skills.

choices.description: The answers its question offers while it waits on one (AskUserQuestion with one question and one answer): one of them is picked by its label (`session.choose`), as a click on it would. nil for any other wait, and once it goes on.

continueAt.description: When Kelp types "continue" into it, if it still stands where the limit left it (`session.continueAt`).

exitCode.description: How its program ended: the exit code, or 128 + the signal that stopped it; nil while it runs.

goal.description: The /goal it works toward (Claude Code checks it after each turn and goes on until it's met); nil without one.

guessed.description: Its status is read off the screen, a guess (an agent without hooks, or one whose hooks went silent): it never says Done on its own nor sends a notification for one. nil: told by the agent itself.

limitHit.description: The plan limit that stopped it; nil again once it does anything else.

origin.description: The session whose program asked for it (`session.create` from inside one, `--outlive` too), as the daemon saw the caller's process, never from what it sent: what an agent starts stays the agent's to act on, and no more than that.

parent.description: The agent that started it (`kelp session new --agent`): it hears how this one is doing and takes it along when it ends.

profile.description: The account profile it started with (Settings › Accounts); nil: the agent's own default login. Kept so a woken or restarted session comes back on the same account.

progress.description: How far what runs in it got, 0–100, when it says (OSC 7501's `progress`, `kelp report`, ConEmu's OSC 9;4).

quietSince.description: Working, but nothing heard from it since then (no hook, or for an agent without hooks no output) for minutes: the sidebar says "quiet 34m" rather than a working ring that tells nothing. nil while news comes.

running.description: The command its shell tool runs now (`AgentCommand`, from its hooks); nil between them.

startedBy.description: The agent a command belongs to (`kelp session new --cmd` inside it): the line under that agent's terminal shows it, instead of a tab and a sidebar row of its own. Unlike a child, it goes on when the agent ends, and gets a tab then.

statusAt.description: When `status` last changed ("working for 4m", "done 2h ago"); nil for sessions from before it was kept.

subagentRuns.description: Its subagents of this turn in the order they started, the finished ones too; follows the two above, ends with the turn.

subagentTasks.description: What each of them does, by the same id, when the agent says (OSC 7501's `title`).

subagents.description: Its own subagents at work now, by id, and what kind each is (its hooks say): they run inside it, with no tab of their own.

summary.description: One-line summary of what the agent did / is asking (local model or hooks).

title.description: Tab title (from the first prompt, or set by hand — a manual name wins).

tmux.description: The tmux session on a remote project's host its agent runs in (`RemoteHost.command(_:inTmux:)`), so the agent outlives a dropped connection and the daemon; kept so a wake or a restart attaches to it again. nil elsewhere, and once Kelp ended that tmux session (Stop, closing the tab).

workDir.description: Where the agent works when it left `cwd` (Claude Code going into its `.claude/worktrees/…`), from its hooks; nil while it works in `cwd`. Paths it prints and its last turn's changes are read there; a restart still starts in `cwd`.

top.description: The biggest three, biggest first; `more` items besides them.

base.description: In Kind's order, the empty ones left out.

setup.description: The base as the agent itself splits it, when it says (Claude Code's /context).

SessionContextParts.Setup.description: What every request starts with, as Claude Code's /context counts it: system prompt, tools, MCP, memory files, skills… (`parts`, in its order, summing to the base), with the biggest items of some ("CLAUDE.md 4k").

buffer.description: Kept free for compacting: the conversation compacts by itself before it reaches this.

deferred.description: Tools it loads only when one is used ("MCP tools (deferred)"): not in the context.

label.description: As Claude Code names it: "System prompt", "Memory files".

cacheUntil.description: When the prompt cache goes cold, by what the last reply wrote to it; nil when that isn't known.

touched.description: When its transcript last changed: a long quiet is a long command, or a subagent that hangs.

SessionTurn.Turn.description: One turn of the agent: what it changed by the time it stopped, and how long it worked.

SessionTurns.Mark.description: A turn's start: `tree` is the folder then (a snapshot in the project's git, which git's cleanup may take after two weeks), `head` its HEAD then.

SessionUsage.Usage.description: CPU (ps's %, summed over the session's processes; 100 = one core) and resident memory of a live session.

SettingsEvent.description: settings.json changed (a set, or the file edited by hand): all of it now.

ShownUI.description: What the app shows, as agents read it back (`kelp ui state`): nothing at all when no app is connected.

commands.description: The palette's commands and the inspector's panels: what `kelp ui command` and `kelp open ext:` take.

focused.description: The focused tab's URI ("" for none).

path.description: Its folder; nil for a built-in.

ShownUI.Item.description: A tab (its URI and title), a command or a panel (its id and title).

Subagent.description: A subagent of an agent's turn, at work or finished. `kind` is empty when only a terminal report told of it.

SubagentStep.description: One thing a subagent did: the tool, and the path or command it was given.

setupNeedsTrust.description: The project's .kelp.yaml has a setup that didn't run: it isn't trusted yet.

activity.description: When someone last typed in it or it printed something.

UIBrowserEvent.description: An agent's `ui.browser`, relayed to the app: it answers with `ui.browser.reply` and the same `request`.

UIEvent.description: An agent's `ui.open` / `ui.command`, relayed to the app: the request's fields and which it was.

Unsynced.description: The newest commits a sync would move: `outgoing` is what a push sends, `incoming` what a pull brings (none without an upstream).

UsageAgents.Agent.description: One agent over the span: its tokens by kind (`input` leaves the cache out) and its own models and projects.

counted.description: The agents whose logs are read, in a fixed order (one not here keeps no counts on this Mac), and those whose own figure is the cost (the rest are priced from list prices). Nil from a kelpd before they were said.

days.description: `days` by day ("yyyy-MM-dd") and agent id; agents and groups most expensive first; `since` is the first day's start.

UsageGet.Block.description: Tokens and their API price over a span (dates as seconds since 1970).

block.description: The 5-hour block now, if one is running.

UsageGet.Codex.description: Codex's own limits from its latest log line (percent used, resets as seconds since 1970).

primaryWindowMinutes.description: Each window's length as Codex says it (nil from an older Codex: then the first is 5 hours, the second a week).

UsageGet.Limit.description: One limit as an agent shows it: kind ("session", "week", "week · Fable"…), percent used, when it resets.

observedAt.description: When a session printed it (Claude's percentages from the last 12 hours); nil for a /usage reading.

plans.description: By agent id: the latest /usage readings, and when they were read.

days.description: Most expensive first; `since` is the first day's start (seconds since 1970).

VMConnection.description: How to run something in a machine: `ssh` and its arguments up to the host, then the command line for the machine's shell, which puts the project folder at the same path inside and goes there.

device.description: An iOS machine's: its simulator's UDID and its runner's port (`ssh` is then xcrun simctl).

VMControl.Action.description: `show`: its screen in a window of its own (a macOS machine's), woken first.

VMDetail.description: What runs in a machine, read from inside (`VMs.detailScript`), with the folders shared with it.

address.description: Its address on the Mac's NAT network: where its ports open from here.

guest.description: A macOS machine's Kelp Guest: whether it may read controls (Accessibility), and whose turn the screen is (kelp-vm says). Nil: not a macOS machine, or Kelp Guest isn't in it. `screenRecording` is no longer asked for: always false.

running.description: False too while Kelp Guest isn't running (its permissions can't be told then).

screen.description: The session whose turn the screen is, while it lasts.

VMDetail.Run.description: A `kelp vm run`: its command ("" for a shell), how long it has run, and the Kelp session that ran it.

connections.description: Commands and shells open in it now.

cpu.description: While it runs: the Mac's CPU it took over the last 5 s, % of one core, as Activity Monitor counts it.

detail.description: While creating, how far ("Downloading Debian 13: 43%"); after an error, what went wrong.

diskMiB.description: Its disk's size on the Mac's disk, MiB.

files.description: A Linux or macOS machine's exchange folder on the Mac, `~/Kelp` inside it (`VMs.filesSetup`).

memoryMiB.description: What it holds of the Mac's memory while it runs (its process's footprint, else its balloon's target), MiB.

sessions.description: The Kelp sessions working in it now: a command running there (`kelp vm run` from an agent or a terminal), or the turn of a macOS machine's screen.

step.description: While it's being made: the step it's at, and how far that step got (0…1) when that's known. `detail` names what it's made from then ("macOS 27.2").

VMMachine.description: A virtual machine Kelp runs for agents on Apple Virtualization: a folder of its own under `<home>/vms/<name>` (its disk, keys, sockets), run by a `kelp-vm` process (the only one with the virtualization entitlement). Agents reach it over SSH through that process (vsock, no network address), each command a connection of its own; it pauses and then sleeps to disk when none is open, and wakes on the next.

os.description: What it is, as the wire and machine.json have it: `linux`, `macos`, `android` or `ios` (`kind`).

rosetta.description: x86-64 Linux programs run through Rosetta (when the Mac has it).

user.description: The account inside: the Mac user's name, so paths and prompts read the same.

VMStep.description: A step of making a machine, as its `creating` file says (`VMMaking`).

WatchTopic.description: What can be watched, and what its key names.

base.description: Branch this one was cut from; when it isn't the repo's base the worktree is part of a PR stack.

issue.description: Links to the task it came from and the PR it became: "#123" / "ENG-123".

madeBy.description: The session whose program made it (`Session.origin`'s kind): an agent works in a workspace it made, across a restart of the daemon too. nil: the user's.

methods.description: The commands its agent ran with its shell tool, oldest first: the last 100, kept while the background service runs.
methods.name: session.commands

methods.description: session.read with room for "Copy Context".
methods.name: session.context

methods.description: What fills a Claude Code conversation's context since its last compaction: the base it starts with (system prompt, tools, CLAUDE.md, skills: the first request) and the parts after it, estimated from the transcript and scaled so that base + parts make the tokens the last reply counted. nil when that isn't known (other agents, no reply yet).
methods.name: session.contextParts

methods.description: How full the agent's conversation is (Claude Code transcripts); nil when that isn't known.
methods.name: session.contextWindow

methods.description: "continue" typed into a session a plan limit stopped, by the daemon, so Kelp's window can be closed by then. nil takes it back.
methods.name: session.continueAt

methods.description: A session in `worktreeId`'s folder, or in `cwd` (which wins): agent `agent`, else the shell command `command`; `tmux`: a terminal attached to that tmux session, started if there is none (see `Tmux`). `parent`: the agent session that started this agent, or this command (see `Session.parent`, `Session.startedBy`), if it is an agent.
methods.name: session.create

methods.description: This connection stops following the session (`session.attach`). The session keeps running.
methods.name: session.detach

methods.description: A new chat beside this one, in the same folder, going on from a copy of its conversation: this one goes on as it was. Claude Code and Codex fork their own (`--fork-session`, `codex fork`); other agents can't, and are refused.
methods.name: session.fork

methods.description: A new agent (`agent`, else the same) in the same workspace, briefed with this one's transcript (`full`: all of it).

methods.description: From a running agent's hooks (`kelp hook`): `event`, and what Claude Code's hook payload says.
methods.name: session.hook

params.description: When the hook ran, on the clock of this boot: hooks arrive out of order when one isn't waited for (a Notification) or a kelpd was away, and a late one says nothing about now.
params.name: at

params.description: `command`: what its shell tool started or finished.
params.name: command

params.description: What the prompt set as a /goal.
params.name: goal

params.description: Stop: the words the turn ended with.
params.name: reply

methods.description: Ends the session.
methods.name: session.kill

methods.description: The agent's last message, from its transcript.
methods.name: session.lastReply

methods.description: All sessions, or those of workspace `worktreeId`.
methods.name: session.list

methods.description: Clears its unread mark.
methods.name: session.markRead

methods.description: Sets its unread mark.
methods.name: session.markUnread

methods.description: To another screen of the same folder: the agent goes on as it was, its tab goes there.
methods.name: session.move

methods.description: A permission question's hook (Claude Code's PermissionRequest) waits here for Allow or Deny given in Kelp: "allow", "deny", or nil once it was answered in the terminal or ten minutes passed. The agent's own menu stays on screen meanwhile (Claude Code shows it while the hook runs), so the terminal can answer too.
methods.name: session.permissionWait

methods.description: The last `bytes` it printed, as text.
methods.name: session.read

methods.description: What a finished Claude Code agent did and what's left, in a line, from a fork of its conversation that leaves the conversation as it was; kept as its summary. nil: not Claude Code, or it couldn't be asked.
methods.name: session.recap

methods.description: Sets its title; an empty one names the session from its task again.
methods.name: session.rename

methods.description: What a program in the session says it's doing (`kelp report`; the same as writing OSC 7501 itself): `state` is idle, working, blocked, done, error or clear; `message` shows on its row's card, `progress` (0–100) on its mark while it works.
methods.name: session.report

methods.description: The size of its terminal.
methods.name: session.resize

methods.description: The same command in the same folder, resuming its conversation unless `resume` is false.
methods.name: session.restart

methods.description: `text`, then Enter (unless `enter` is false) a beat later so a TUI takes it as a submit.
methods.name: session.send

methods.description: `kelp attach`'s first line: from here on the connection is the session's terminal, raw bytes both ways (its history and output out, the user's typing in), and no JSON-RPC. A paused session wakes at `cols` × `rows`; an ended one shows what it last printed, then the connection ends.
methods.name: session.stream

methods.description: All a subagent did and what it reported, read from its transcript; nil when there is none.
methods.name: session.subagentJournal

methods.description: What an agent's subagents at work did last, by id. Empty for an agent that keeps no transcript of them: only Claude Code does.
methods.name: session.subagentSteps

methods.description: What a session's status went through and the hooks it heard, oldest first, a line each. Kept after it ended; empty when nothing happened yet.
methods.name: session.trail

methods.description: → {turn, hasBase}: the files its last turn changed and how long it took; null when the session isn't running.
methods.name: session.turn

methods.description: The last `session.turnUndo` taken back: the folder as it was before it, while it is still `state` (the Plan that undo answered with). `turn` is the one that was undone.
methods.name: session.turnRedo

Without `apply`, what would go back and the folder's state now; with it, done only while the folder is still that `state`, answering with the state after (for `session.turnRedo`). Refused while the agent works, after commits since the turn began, and with another agent in the folder. `.env` files stay as they are.
methods.name: session.turnUndo

methods.description: The session's turns, the newest first (the last 20): how its folder was as each began, with the prompt that started it. None for a remote project's, where no snapshots are taken.
methods.name: session.turns

methods.description: CPU and memory of each running session's processes.
methods.name: session.usage

methods.description: A running session's status and where it came from: a hook, the program's own report, the screen. nil: it isn't running.
methods.name: session.why

methods.description: The user's keys (`base64`), or `text` as it is.
methods.name: session.write

methods.description: All settings (settings.json's keys, flat and dotted).
methods.name: settings.get

methods.description: A null `value` resets the key → all settings.
methods.name: settings.set

methods.description: Whether a new Claude Code chat in this workspace gets Kelp's browser skill, and why: `agents.skills.browser` (auto / on / off), laid under the project's own choice (UI state `browser.choice.<repo>`: "on" / "off").
methods.name: skills.browser

methods.description: What the app restores (`UIState`): `key` → its value or null; `prefix` → {key: value} for every key that starts with it.
methods.name: state.get

methods.name: state.set

methods.description: The tmux sessions on the workspace's machine (a remote project's host), the last used first; none while tmux runs no server there.
methods.name: tmux.list

methods.description: `kelp browser`: `action` (a `BrowserAction`) on the browser tab of workspace `worktreeId`, done by the app, whose answer is the result. It waits for the page, up to `wait` seconds.
methods.name: ui.browser

methods.description: The app's answer to `event.ui.browser` (its `request`): the result, or what went wrong. Only Kelp's window.
methods.name: ui.browser.reply

methods.description: Runs the app's command `id` (as in the palette) with `args`.
methods.name: ui.command

methods.description: A tab for `uri` in the app: beside the focused one (`split` right|down), in workspace `worktreeId`; `focus` brings Kelp forward and shows that workspace.
methods.name: ui.open

methods.description: What the app shows (workspace, tabs, extensions, commands), for agents to read back with `ui.state`. Only Kelp's window.
methods.name: ui.publish

methods.description: What the app last published (an empty object when no app is connected).
methods.name: ui.state

methods.description: What each agent used over `days`, read from its own logs on this Mac (Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Kimi Code, Copilot): by day and agent, and by agent, model and project, priced as the API would (Grok as it says itself; 0 for a model with no list price).
methods.name: usage.agents

methods.description: Per account: Claude's 5-hour block, today and the week; Codex's limits (cached for a minute unless `force`); the plan limits the agents' own /usage screens show.
methods.name: usage.get

methods.description: What Claude Code used over `days`, by day, model and project, priced as the API would.
methods.name: usage.report

methods.description: Changes a Linux or macOS machine's processors, memory (GB) and disk (GB, only larger: Linux grows into it as it boots) while it's shut down. The user's: what every chat's machine has, and the Mac's memory.
methods.name: vm.configure

methods.description: What `kelp vm run` needs to run a command in it, in `cwd`'s project folder (shared with the machine at the same path); with no `cwd`, in its own home folder, nothing shared.
methods.name: vm.connect

methods.description: `start` boots or wakes it; `sleep` saves it to disk (its memory freed, what ran inside goes on when it wakes); `stop` shuts it down (what ran inside ends); `delete` stops it and removes it, its disk and all. Stop and delete are the user's.
methods.name: vm.control

methods.description: Makes a machine: downloads its image the first time (checked against the distribution's checksums), then its disk and first boot. Answers at once, `creating`; `vm.list` follows it.
methods.name: vm.create

params.description: Memory in GiB, disk in GiB.
params.name: cpus

params.description: A file of the user's to make it from instead of downloading: macOS's restore image (.ipsw), or a Linux cloud image's raw disk (cloud-init sets its account up, as Debian's).
params.name: file

methods.description: What runs in a running machine; nil while it isn't running (reading never wakes it).
methods.name: vm.detail

methods.description: The machines and their state.
methods.name: vm.list

methods.description: A machine's screen, read and driven by the daemon: `args` as `kelp vm` takes them, ["screenshot", "/abs/file.png"], ["click", "X", "Y", "--right"?, "--double"?], ["move", "X", "Y"], ["drag", "X", "Y", "X2", "Y2"], ["scroll", "DY", "X"?, "Y"?], ["type", "TEXT"], ["key", "cmd+space"], ["press", "REF|TITLE"]; an Android or iOS one's also ["install", "/abs/app"], ["launch", "ID"], ["open", "URL"]. A macOS machine's from the Mac's side (no permission inside it), points of its 1280 × 800 screen, clicks, keys and scrolls taking turns by `session`; an Android one's through adb, in its screen's pixels; an iOS one's through Kelp's runner, in points.
methods.name: vm.screen

methods.description: Types into a macOS machine's screen. `text` nil: the machine's password (from the Keychain), for a dialog inside that asks for it (Privacy & Security, an installer).
methods.name: vm.type

methods.description: The controls on a machine's screen, a line each, indented, with a ref to press (`kelp vm ui`): a macOS machine's front app (or `app`'s) through Kelp Guest inside it, an Android one's through uiautomator, an iOS one's through Kelp's runner (`app`: a bundle id).
methods.name: vm.ui
